newsitem.title: UK: UK to seek reform of EU farming, fishing policy.
newsitem.headline: UK to seek reform of EU farming, fishing policy.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government said on Wednesday it will look to reform the European Union's agriculture and fisheries policies.

It said the Common Agricultural Policy needed to be changed to phase out quotas and subsidies while the problem of quota hoppers fishing in British waters would be addressed at the EU intergovernmental conference summit in June.

"(My government) will seek further reform of the Common Agricultural Policy to secure lower food prices for consumers and save money, support the rural economy and enhance the environment," a speech written for Queen Elizabeth said.
The speech, written by cabinet ministers, was delivered to formally open parliament after Labour's landslide win at May 1 elections.
"They will seek changes to the Common Fisheries Policy to conserve fish stocks in the long-term interest of the UK fishing industry," the speech said.
A government note tacked on to the speech said Britain wanted more cuts in support to farmers to bring EU prices closer to the world market, with the aim of boosting exports without using subsidies.
"As this happens, the present widespread use of supply control measures such as quotas and set-aside should become redundant," the note said.
Reducing intervention would benefit farmers, consumers and taxpayers it said.

Turning to fisheries, the note said quota hoppers -- non-UK fishing vessels which fish in British waters having purchased licenses from British fishermen -- would be tackled at next month's summit in Amsterdam.
"The government has made it clear that this issue must be addressed at the highest level," it said.

The note said the new Labour government has inherited decisions made last year requiring cuts in fishing effort of up to 30 percent over five years. "We want early discussions about how to implement these tough decisions," the note said.
